rounds.title: Seed Of The Woman
rounds.answer: Christ's victory over sin and death
acceptedAnswers: Christ's victory over sin and death
clues: This prophecy belongs to the victory theme.
The Old Testament reference is Genesis 3:15.
The wording includes: "It shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel."
A New Testament connection appears at Hebrews 2:14.
The fulfillment wording includes: "That through death he might destroy him that had the power of death."
rounds.teachingNote: This is commonly read by Christian interpreters as an early promise of victory over evil.

rounds.title: Blessing To All Nations
clues: This prophecy belongs to the nations theme.
The Old Testament reference is Genesis 12:3.
The wording includes: "In thee shall all families of the earth be blessed."
A New Testament connection appears at Galatians 3:8.
The fulfillment wording includes: "In thee shall all nations be blessed."
rounds.teachingNote: The New Testament explicitly applies this Abraham promise to the gospel going to the nations.

rounds.title: Ruler From Judah
clues: This prophecy belongs to the kingship theme.
The Old Testament reference is Genesis 49:10.
The wording includes: "The sceptre shall not depart from Judah."
A New Testament connection appears at Hebrews 7:14.
The fulfillment wording includes: "Our Lord sprang out of Juda."
rounds.teachingNote: The Judah connection is a widely recognized messianic theme.

rounds.title: Prophet Like Moses
clues: This prophecy belongs to the prophet theme.
The Old Testament reference is Deuteronomy 18:15.
The wording includes: "The Lord thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet."
A New Testament connection appears at Acts 3:22.
The fulfillment wording includes: "A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you."
rounds.teachingNote: Acts gives this passage a direct place in apostolic preaching about Jesus.

rounds.title: Son And King
clues: This prophecy belongs to the kingship theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 2:7.
The wording includes: "Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee."
A New Testament connection appears at Acts 13:33.
The fulfillment wording includes: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee."
rounds.teachingNote: Psalm 2 is used in the New Testament to speak of the Messiah's sonship and reign.

rounds.title: Not Seeing Corruption
clues: This prophecy belongs to the resurrection theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 16:10.
The wording includes: "Neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption."
A New Testament connection appears at Acts 2:31.
The fulfillment wording includes: "His soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption."
rounds.teachingNote: Acts 2 directly connects Psalm 16 with the resurrection of Jesus.

rounds.title: Suffering Cry
rounds.answer: Jesus' suffering cry from the cross
acceptedAnswers: Jesus' suffering cry from the cross
clues: This prophecy belongs to the suffering theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 22:1.
The wording includes: "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"
A New Testament connection appears at Matthew 27:46.
The fulfillment wording includes: "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"
rounds.teachingNote: The Gospel records Jesus using Psalm 22 language during the crucifixion.

rounds.title: Garments Divided
clues: This prophecy belongs to the suffering theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 22:18.
The wording includes: "They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture."
A New Testament connection appears at John 19:24.
The fulfillment wording includes: "They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it."
rounds.teachingNote: John explicitly cites the casting of lots as fulfillment of scripture.

rounds.title: Bones Not Broken
clues: This prophecy belongs to the suffering theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 34:20.
The wording includes: "He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken."
A New Testament connection appears at John 19:36.
The fulfillment wording includes: "A bone of him shall not be broken."
rounds.teachingNote: John cites this detail while describing Jesus' death.

rounds.title: Betrayed By A Friend
clues: This prophecy belongs to the betrayal theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 41:9.
The wording includes: "Mine own familiar friend... hath lifted up his heel against me."
A New Testament connection appears at John 13:18.
The fulfillment wording includes: "He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me."
rounds.teachingNote: John records Jesus citing the psalm in the context of Judas's betrayal.

rounds.title: Zeal For God's House
clues: This prophecy belongs to the temple theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 69:9.
The wording includes: "The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up."
A New Testament connection appears at John 2:17.
The fulfillment wording includes: "The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up."
rounds.teachingNote: John presents the temple cleansing through the lens of Psalm 69.

rounds.title: Vinegar Given
clues: This prophecy belongs to the suffering theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 69:21.
The wording includes: "In my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink."
A New Testament connection appears at John 19:29.
The fulfillment wording includes: "They filled a spunge with vinegar... and put it to his mouth."
rounds.teachingNote: The Gospels connect this detail with Jesus' crucifixion.

rounds.title: At God's Right Hand
clues: This prophecy belongs to the exaltation theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 110:1.
The wording includes: "Sit thou at my right hand."
A New Testament connection appears at Hebrews 1:13.
The fulfillment wording includes: "Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool."
rounds.teachingNote: Psalm 110 is one of the New Testament's most frequent messianic texts.

rounds.title: Rejected Stone
clues: This prophecy belongs to the rejection theme.
The Old Testament reference is Psalm 118:22.
The wording includes: "The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone."
A New Testament connection appears at Acts 4:11.
The fulfillment wording includes: "The stone which was set at nought of you builders."
rounds.teachingNote: Acts directly applies the stone image to Jesus' rejection and exaltation.

rounds.title: Virgin-Born Sign
clues: This prophecy belongs to the birth theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 7:14.
The wording includes: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son."
A New Testament connection appears at Matthew 1:23.
The fulfillment wording includes: "They shall call his name Emmanuel."
rounds.teachingNote: Matthew explicitly quotes Isaiah 7:14 in the infancy narrative.

rounds.title: Light In Galilee
clues: This prophecy belongs to the ministry theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 9:1-2.
The wording includes: "The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light."
A New Testament connection appears at Matthew 4:15-16.
The fulfillment wording includes: "The people which sat in darkness saw great light."
rounds.teachingNote: The Gospel citation ties the prophecy to Jesus' public ministry in Galilee.

rounds.title: Child And Kingdom
clues: This prophecy belongs to the kingship theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 9:6-7.
The wording includes: "Unto us a child is born... and the government shall be upon his shoulder."
A New Testament connection appears at Luke 1:32-33.
The fulfillment wording includes: "He shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever."
rounds.teachingNote: Luke's announcement uses Davidic kingdom language that Christians connect with Isaiah's promise.

rounds.title: Voice In The Wilderness
clues: This prophecy belongs to the forerunner theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 40:3.
The wording includes: "Prepare ye the way of the Lord."
A New Testament connection appears at Matthew 3:3.
The fulfillment wording includes: "The voice of one crying in the wilderness."
rounds.teachingNote: The Synoptic Gospels connect Isaiah 40:3 with John the Baptist.

rounds.title: Chosen Servant
clues: This prophecy belongs to the servant theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 42:1-4.
The wording includes: "Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect."
A New Testament connection appears at Matthew 12:18-21.
The fulfillment wording includes: "Behold my servant, whom I have chosen."
rounds.teachingNote: Matthew's quotation presents Jesus' ministry through Isaiah's servant language.

rounds.title: Despised And Rejected
clues: This prophecy belongs to the suffering theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 53:3.
The wording includes: "He is despised and rejected of men."
A New Testament connection appears at John 1:11.
The fulfillment wording includes: "He came unto his own, and his own received him not."
rounds.teachingNote: This pairing is thematic rather than a direct quotation, so the wording stays careful.

rounds.title: Wounded For Transgressions
clues: This prophecy belongs to the suffering theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 53:5.
The wording includes: "He was wounded for our transgressions."
A New Testament connection appears at 1 Peter 2:24.
The fulfillment wording includes: "By whose stripes ye were healed."
rounds.teachingNote: 1 Peter explicitly uses Isaiah 53 language for Christ's suffering.

rounds.title: Silent Before Accusers
clues: This prophecy belongs to the suffering theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 53:7.
The wording includes: "He opened not his mouth."
A New Testament connection appears at Matthew 27:14.
The fulfillment wording includes: "He answered him to never a word."
rounds.teachingNote: The Gospel scene is a widely recognized fulfillment connection to Isaiah 53.

rounds.title: With The Rich In Death
clues: This prophecy belongs to the death theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 53:9.
The wording includes: "With the rich in his death."
A New Testament connection appears at Matthew 27:57-60.
The fulfillment wording includes: "A rich man of Arimathaea... laid it in his own new tomb."
rounds.teachingNote: Matthew's burial account is commonly read with Isaiah 53:9.

rounds.title: Numbered With Transgressors
clues: This prophecy belongs to the suffering theme.
The Old Testament reference is Isaiah 53:12.
The wording includes: "He was numbered with the transgressors."
A New Testament connection appears at Luke 22:37.
The fulfillment wording includes: "He was reckoned among the transgressors."
rounds.teachingNote: Luke records Jesus explicitly quoting this line about what must be accomplished.

rounds.title: Bethlehem Ruler
clues: This prophecy belongs to the birth theme.
The Old Testament reference is Micah 5:2.
The wording includes: "Out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel."
A New Testament connection appears at Matthew 2:1-6.
The fulfillment wording includes: "In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet."
rounds.teachingNote: Matthew directly links Messiah's birthplace with Micah 5:2.
